symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A tenant_scope context manager restores the prior scope on __exit__ and is safe to reuse/re-enter.
symptom_spec.observable: __exit__ used .take().flatten(), collapsing 'never entered' (None) and 'entered-while-unscoped' (Some(None)) into one unbind arm, so a stray exit cleared a live tenant scope — a data-scope leak on green CI.
symptom_spec.control: Match the full Option<Option<TenantId>>: Some(Some(t))->restore, Some(None)->unbind, None->no-op; refuse re-entry. Assert a stray exit on a never-entered scope leaves a live scope intact.

which_gate_missed: adversarial-audit (states-the-happy-path-test-never-constructs lens: re-entry/reuse/never-entered)

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: The remote publish_topic path byte-matches the embedded path for any table.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An over-fetch cap bounds only the excluded k-hop headroom, leaving the requested k uncapped.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A regression head reaches a high-offset / large-magnitude target within the training budget.
symptom_spec.observable: The design rescaled the loss instead of standardizing the data; under Adam (param step ~lr regardless of loss scale) the mean stayed near the zero-init (~2163 off) and the variance floored.
symptom_spec.control: A high-offset oracle per trainable head: standardize the target into ~[-3,3] in data space with a persisted de-standardization affine; assert the served mean reaches the target magnitude.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: The negative control proves the un-standardized path still collapses (oracle exercises the bug).
symptom_spec.observable: The control asserted 'mean far OR sigma floored', but the un-standardized path diverged to NaN, and NaN>100 || NaN<0.05 is false||false — a divergence read as a successful fit, so the control flaked.
symptom_spec.control: Make 'failed to fit' include non-finite (NaN/±inf counts as collapse), or seed the run deterministically.

which_gate_missed: fix-verifier non-finite-control check (a control that passes on the unmodelled failure mode is tautological)

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A linear-decay learning-rate schedule floors at 0 at and past its horizon.
symptom_spec.observable: Past the horizon the LR went negative (gradient ascent) because the horizon undercounted realized optimizer steps (ignored each epoch's trailing grad-accumulation flush), so progress>1 and lr0*(1-progress)<0.
symptom_spec.control: Count realized steps incl. accumulation flushes; clamp progress to [0,1]; floor the rate at 0; add a boundary oracle evaluating the schedule past its horizon.

which_gate_missed: ai-model boundary/degenerate oracle (domain-validity at the numeric edge)

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An undirected edge contributes once to each endpoint's degree.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: resolve_embedding_table returns the temporally-newest ready model embedding table for a source, correctly and identically on SQLite and Postgres.
symptom_spec.observable: The resolver tie-broke equal created_at with SQLite-only `rowid DESC`; on Postgres this hard-errors at plan time (SQLSTATE 42703, column "rowid" does not exist), so on a Postgres-backed catalog deployment the resolver fails at plan time and embedding-table resolution never completes. Invisible on SQLite, which has a rowid; the existing resolver tests ran SQLite-only, so the gap shipped latent.
symptom_spec.control: Order by an app-supplied full-resolution backend-identical created_at (backend::now_sortable) with table_name as a nanosecond-collision-only tiebreak; the both-backends test uses adversarially-named tables (older model 'zzz', newer model 'aaa') so a table_name-order tiebreak returns the wrong row, and the Postgres arm bites the rowid hard-error.

which_gate_missed: backend-parity — the catalog/store it-suite ran on SQLite only; SQLite's permissive rowid masked a Postgres-strictness violation (the E-class root the v0.43.0 Postgres matrix closes)

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: probe_cache_record returns a sound reusable table whenever ANY ready row with the exact (definition_hash, input_anchors) has an extant artifact — not only when the single first-selected candidate does.
symptom_spec.observable: find_ready_result_tables_by_definition ordered candidates created_at ASC and lookup_cached returned only the first (oldest) exact-anchor match; probe_cache_record checked artifact existence on that one row with no fallthrough, so when a producer recomputed an identical (definition,inputs) key and the selected match's bytes were reaped while another match's were intact, the probe returned None — a false cache-miss and needless recompute. Not Postgres-specific; invisible on per-test SQLite catalogs that never accumulate two same-key ready rows, surfaced by the shared-Postgres it-matrix.
symptom_spec.control: Select exact-anchor-match candidates newest-first and return the first with an extant artifact; None only if none survive. Tested on both backends with >=2 same-key ready rows, reaping the preferred candidate's artifact and asserting the reuse still resolves — plus a case proving a DESC-only change without the fallthrough iteration would still miss.

which_gate_missed: backend-parity — the freshness cache-reuse path only ran on per-test SQLite catalogs that never accumulate two ready rows sharing a definition/anchor key, so the first-match-no-retry gap was unobservable until the shared-Postgres it-matrix

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A correctly-bound tenant session reading a result table over any name-addressable lane (Flight db.sql, gRPC sql) resolves only result tables whose catalog tenant_id matches its bound tenant plus tenant_id IS NULL global tables; naming another tenant's private result table resolves to not-found / zero rows — the same organizational disjointness get_result_table and the mutable-table lane already enforce (B5). This completes an existing ORGANIZATIONAL tenant-scope mechanism; it is NOT a hostile-principal security boundary — the trusted-network posture is unchanged.
symptom_spec.observable: On one engine (shared SessionContext) with tenants A and B correctly bound, tenant A materializes result table jammi.<tableA> with N rows (asof_join or any result-producing verb; measured N=79615). Tenant B, bound to B, issues SELECT count(*) FROM "jammi.<tableA>" over the db.sql lane; the analyzer injects no predicate (result Parquet has no tenant_id column, tenant_scope.rs:283-291) and the table is registered globally into the one shared context (store/mod.rs:1212-1247), so it returns N (tenant A's full table) instead of 0. Secondary: the result-table schema/name enumeration surfaces <tableA> to tenant B.
symptom_spec.control: Three arms in the SAME test: (1) OWN-TENANT VISIBILITY — tenant A (correctly bound) reading jammi.<tableA> STILL returns its N rows (a fix that over-scopes to invisibility is wrong). (2) GLOBAL-STILL-VISIBLE — a result table with catalog tenant_id IS NULL remains visible (nonzero) to BOTH tenants (fix must not over-scope NULL-tenant global tables). (3) NON-VACUOUS RED — the tenant-B zero must be a SCOPING zero not a load/empty/error artifact: the identical query returns N under an admin/unscoped or owning-tenant read in the same test. Passing shape: N for owning/admin read AND 0 for cross-tenant read.

which_gate_missed: tenant-isolation oracle at the data-scan altitude — the existing FlightSql oracle case drives a MUTABLE table (which isolates via the provider's backend-SQL predicate) and never exercises a result-table Parquet scan, so the result-table lane's missing organizational scope was unobserved. Root: analyzer injects a tenant predicate only on scans declaring a tenant_id column; result Parquets carry none.
